name: mirage
text: Not tax advice. It's less of a nightmare than it sounds, because you don't list bets one by one. The IRS wants totals: total winnings and total losses for the year (and for losses a log or statement backing it up). Thousands of bets just means you need the totals to come from a statement, not by hand. Practical plan: (1) Ask Novig Live Chat for a trading history statement for each tax year; it's one request. (2) Use the app's saved bets as a cross-check: I can add a one-tap yearly export (winnings total, losses total, fees, by month) from the Tracker data so you have both numbers ready. (3) Hand those two totals to a preparer; with totals it's a short job. The real risk isn't the volume, it's whether the 90% loss limit and itemizing leave you owing tax on a break-even year, which is why a preparer is worth the fee at your volume. Want me to build that yearly export now?
